clue.text: Hackers heard in the Treasury?

indicators.note: something heard is taken by its sound rather than its spelling

blocks.note: people with a hacking cough are coughers

explanation.surface: Computer criminals are rumoured to have broken into the government's finance department.
explanation.walkthrough: Hackers looks like computer intruders, but here they are people with a hacking cough.
explanation.definitionFit: Coffers are strongboxes, and by extension the funds or treasury of a state or organisation.

clue.text: It protects the shoulder during a caper

indicators.note: during means within the span of the following word, so the letters sit inside it

blocks.note: the first four letters of the word

explanation.surface: Some padding guards a shoulder while someone carries out a daring escapade.
explanation.definitionFit: A cape is a sleeveless cloak worn over the shoulders, covering and sheltering them.

clue.text: Buddy in a boa or a bird?

blocks.note: a pal dressed in a feather boa is a friend with feathers on
a jocular phrase for any bird

explanation.walkthrough: A boa here is a feathery scarf, not a snake; the playful phrase covers both a friend so dressed and a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a familiar humorous name for a bird, and literally describes a companion wearing plumage.

clue.text: Turning pale and half seen to pass away

indicators.note: turning suggests the letters are spun round into a new order
half means only part of the word is kept and the rest dropped

blocks.note: taken as written, then cut to its first half

explanation.surface: Someone goes white and is half-glimpsed as they die.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pass away' reads as dying, but the answer is what time does when it passes.
explanation.definitionFit: Time that elapses slips by or goes past, which is one sense of passing away.

clue.text: He takes black powder to calm down

indicators.note: takes means one part picks up the other alongside it, placing them side by side

blocks.note: the black powder left by fire

explanation.surface: A man swallows a dark powder as a sedative.
explanation.definitionFit: To soothe someone is to pacify or settle them, making them less agitated.

clue.text: English actress turns odd, extending sins

indicators.note: turns suggests the letters are twisted into another order
extending means lengthening a word by pushing extra letters into it

blocks.note: taken as written, then split open
taken as written, then rearranged and placed after the second letter of sins

explanation.surface: A British stage star goes strange, adding to her wrongdoings.
explanation.walkthrough: Sarah Siddons was the great tragic actress of the late 18th-century London stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Sarah Siddons was a celebrated English tragedian, famous as Lady Macbeth at Drury Lane.

clue.text: I'm mixing with crooks in the sanatorium

indicators.note: mixing stirs the letters together into a new order

explanation.surface: A patient confesses to socialising with criminals while in a convalescent home.
explanation.definitionFit: A sickroom is a room set aside for ill people, as a sanatorium is a place for them.

clue.text: Training of horses makes my costume seem older

blocks.note: to age is to look or grow older

explanation.surface: Someone complains that riding lessons make their outfit look old-fashioned.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressage is the equestrian discipline of schooling horses to perform precise movements.

clue.text: Simmering is low priority

blocks.note: first meaning: a pan left on a rear ring of the stove to cook gently
second meaning: set aside for later attention

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like a kitchen tip; the phrase describes both a gently cooking pot and a postponed task.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom comes from cooking: a pot moved to a rear hob simmers unattended, as a deferred matter waits.

clue.text: Sing about the subject a bit

indicators.note: about means going around something, enclosing it

blocks.note: taken as written, then split around the other part
subject matter: the topic under discussion

explanation.surface: A chorister is told to sing a little about the topic.
explanation.definitionFit: A smattering is a small amount or slight knowledge of something, just a little.

clue.text: Square-shaped A to Z, a record sent back

indicators.note: sent back means returned to where it started, so the string is read from the end

blocks.note: the two letters at the ends of the range

explanation.surface: A square street guide and a disc are returned to sender.
explanation.walkthrough: An A to Z is a British street atlas, which makes the surface plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaza is a public square or open marketplace in a town, especially in Spanish-speaking places.

clue.text: Partly scorches tray-cloth, just the band

indicators.note: partly means only a portion of the following words is used, a run lying within them

blocks.note: the letters run from the third of the first word into the second word

explanation.surface: An iron slightly burns the tray-cloth, just a strip of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' looks like a strip of the cloth, but it is the musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchestra is a large group of musicians playing together, a band in the broad sense.

clue.text: The person's chop will be cooked, if it's luminous

indicators.note: cooking transforms ingredients, so these letters are mixed into something new

explanation.surface: Someone's lamb chop will be cooked if it glows.
explanation.definitionFit: Phosphorescent things give off light without burning, so they glow and are luminous.

clue.text: This is with regard to one's following

blocks.note: first meaning: a preposition, concerning or about
second meaning: obeying or honouring rules or wishes

explanation.walkthrough: 'Following' sounds like a band of supporters, but it is the verb sense of abiding by a rule.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a preposition meaning concerning and a participle meaning honouring or abiding by.

clue.text: Aristocrat almost before his time?

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is left off

explanation.surface: A nobleman nearly turns up too soon, or was ahead of his era.
explanation.definitionFit: An earl is a British nobleman ranking between a marquess and a viscount.

clue.text: Highbrow or hippie?

blocks.note: first meaning: an intellectual, especially one devoted to classical music
second meaning: a counterculture type with flowing locks

explanation.walkthrough: The intellectual sense comes from the stereotype of the shaggy-maned classical musician or professor.
explanation.definitionFit: Both an aesthete with artistic tastes and a flower-power drop-out wear their tresses unshorn, giving one label.

clue.text: 100 move slowly round small monastery

indicators.note: round means wrapping around something, enclosing it

explanation.surface: A hundred monks shuffle around a little religious house.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloister is a covered walk in a religious house, and by extension a monastery or convent itself.

clue.text: Three rulers try to hold rocking chair

indicators.note: rocking shakes things back and forth, so the letters are jumbled
to hold means to keep something within, enclosing it

blocks.note: taken as written, split around the other part

explanation.surface: Three monarchs attempt to keep a rocking chair steady.
explanation.definitionFit: A triarchy is government by three people jointly, or the trio of rulers themselves.

clue.text: Those who wade quietly, getting left among the snakes

indicators.note: among means placed in the middle of something, surrounded by it

blocks.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for soft

explanation.surface: Waders creep quietly through water and end up stranded among snakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Paddlers walk barefoot in shallow water, which is wading.

clue.text: Complexion of second family

explanation.surface: Someone asks about the colouring of a second relative.
explanation.definitionFit: Complexion means the tone and texture of a person's face, which is their skin.

clue.text: Nelly beheaded about six with malice

indicators.note: beheaded means the head, the opening letter, is cut off
about means going around something, enclosing it

explanation.surface: Nelly is spitefully decapitated, with half a dozen others involved.
explanation.definitionFit: To act evilly is to act wickedly, with ill will or malice.

clue.text: Cow found beneath wrecked car in Poland

definitions.note: a city in Poland, not the country

indicators.note: something wrecked is smashed up, so the letters are broken and reassembled
in a down entry, a part found beneath another is written after it

explanation.surface: A cow is discovered trapped under a crashed car on a Polish road.
explanation.walkthrough: Cracow is the older English spelling of Krakow, the historic city in southern Poland.
explanation.definitionFit: Cracow, now usually written Krakow, is a major city located in southern Poland.

clue.text: Key moral quality seen in divine rural act

indicators.note: seen in signals the letters are visible within the phrase, though not in the order printed

explanation.surface: A central ethical principle is observed in a holy country deed.
explanation.definitionFit: The cardinal virtues are the four chief moral qualities: prudence, justice, temperance and fortitude; cardinal means principal.

clue.text: She hides ring in footwear

indicators.note: hides means keeps something out of sight inside itself

blocks.note: taken as written, split around the other part
a ring is round like the letter

explanation.surface: A woman conceals a ring in her shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoe is a piece of footwear, one item of what is worn on the feet.

clue.text: Oddly, I can't idle like this twin

indicators.note: oddly means in a strange way, so the letters come out in an unusual order

explanation.surface: One twin says, strangely, that they cannot laze about like their sibling.
explanation.definitionFit: Identical twins come from one egg; twin used as an adjective means matching exactly.

clue.text: Commander-in-chief goes to hospital: it's easy

indicators.note: goes to means one part moves up next to the next, so they are set side by side

explanation.surface: The top general is admitted to hospital, but the treatment is simple.
explanation.definitionFit: A cinch is an informal word for a task that is very simple or certain.

clue.text: He turns dog on Freya nearly

indicators.note: turns means the letters are spun into another order
nearly means not quite complete, so the last letter is lost

explanation.surface: A man sets his dog on a woman called Freya, almost.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is just 'He': Godfrey is a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Godfrey is a traditional male first name, so any Godfrey can be referred to as he.

clue.text: Right inside running wet eye is growth making a bow

indicators.note: running means flowing loose, so the letters are set in motion and rearranged
inside means placed within something else

explanation.surface: A tearful, streaming eye produces a stye that makes someone bow their head.
explanation.walkthrough: English longbows were traditionally made from yew wood.
explanation.definitionFit: A yew tree is a growth whose springy wood was the classic material for longbows.
